sources.title: Address registration after moving — synthetic summary

passages.text: Synthetic summary: a person who moves into a dwelling in Germany is generally expected to register the new address with the local registration office within a short period after moving in. This demo uses 14 days as an illustrative period.
Synthetic summary: registration usually requires a valid identity document such as a passport and a confirmation from the landlord (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) that the person moved in.
Synthetic summary: after registration a confirmation of registration is issued. Other services, such as the tax identification number, typically follow registration.

sources.title: Family benefit eligibility — synthetic summary (older revision)

passages.text: Synthetic summary: a family benefit may be available to parents who live in Germany and whose child lives in their household. The child's age and education status can affect eligibility.
Synthetic summary: applicants are typically asked for proof of residence, the child's birth certificate and a tax identification number.
Synthetic summary: a person who disagrees with a benefit decision can usually file an objection within one month of receiving the decision.

sources.title: Health insurance on arrival — synthetic summary

passages.text: Synthetic summary: residents in Germany are generally required to hold health insurance. Employees are usually enrolled through their employer; others choose a statutory or private insurer.
Synthetic summary: proof of health insurance is often requested for residence permits, employment and study enrolment.

sources.title: Residence permits for non-EU nationals — synthetic overview

passages.text: Synthetic overview: nationals of countries outside the EU usually need a residence title for stays longer than 90 days. The type of title depends on the purpose, such as employment, study or family reunification.
Synthetic overview: applicants are commonly asked for a passport, biometric photo, proof of health insurance and documents about the purpose of stay. A human case officer decides.

rule_sets.name: Address registration obligation after moving (Berlin, illustrative)

label.en: Are you moving into a home in Berlin?
label.de: Ziehen Sie in eine Wohnung in Berlin?

label.en: How many months do you plan to stay?
label.de: Wie viele Monate möchten Sie bleiben?

label.en: Are you already registered at this address?
label.de: Sind Sie bereits unter dieser Adresse gemeldet?

all.explain: Registration relates to moving into a dwelling.
This illustrative rule uses a stay of 3 months or more.
You are not registered at the address yet.

outcomes.likely_applicable: Registration of your address likely applies. The illustrative period used here is 14 days after moving in.
outcomes.likely_not_applicable: Based on your answers, this illustrative registration rule may not apply. Check with the office if unsure.

versions.appeal_guidance: Registration is not a discretionary decision. If the office refuses registration, ask for the reasons in writing.

label.en: Does the child live in your household?
label.de: Lebt das Kind in Ihrem Haushalt?

label.en: Does the child live in your household?
label.de: Lebt das Kind in Ihrem Haushalt?

label.en: Do you have a German tax identification number?
label.he: האם יש לך מספר זיהוי מס גרמני?

all.explain: The illustrative rule requires residence in Germany.
The child must live in your household.
This illustrative version uses an age limit of under 18.
A tax identification number is usually requested.

outcomes.likely_applicable: Based on this illustrative rule, a family benefit may be available. Only the authority can decide.
outcomes.likely_not_applicable: This illustrative rule may not fit your answers. This is not a refusal: you can still ask the authority for a decision.

versions.appeal_guidance: Illustrative: an objection can usually be filed within one month of receiving a decision. CivicBridge links the appeal to your case.
